cards.explanation: The answer is encourages. Paul sends for the disciples, and after encouraging them, he says goodbye and leaves for Macedonia (Acts 20:1). He doesn't just slip out the back door after all that uproar. I think a little encouragement is a fine thing to leave behind, friends.

The answer is that the Jews form a plot against him. Paul is about to sail for Syria when the Jews form a plot against him, so he decides to go back through Macedonia (Acts 20:3). Plans change, and Paul changes with them. I've had a batch plan fall apart, friends, but never over a plot like that.

The answer is the Feast of Unleavened Bread. The writer says, "…after the Feast of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi…" (Acts 20:6). Notice the "we" again, so the writer is on the boat too. I like a feast with a clear start and finish, friends. It makes planning easier.

The answer is that he's ready to leave the next day. The text says that since Paul was ready to leave the next day, he talked to them and kept on speaking until midnight (Acts 20:7). I think he had a lot to fit in before the road called him away. Midnight, friends. I've never kept an oven on that long without somebody yelling about the bill.

The answer is True. The text says Eutychus, seated in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on (Acts 20:9). I think a window seat is a risky spot to get sleepy. Hold onto that detail, friends, because it matters in a moment.

The answer is False. The text says Eutychus fell from the third story and "…was picked up dead." (Acts 20:9). He wasn't just shaken up. I think this part of the story hurts, friends, so it's worth slowing down here. The story isn't over, though.

The answer is that the young man is still alive. Paul says, "Do not be alarmed!" and then, "He is still alive!" (Acts 20:10). He goes down, throws himself on the young man and embraces him. Then he speaks, friends, and what he says is good news for everybody in that room.

The answer is that he keeps speaking until daybreak. After going back upstairs, breaking bread and eating, Paul speaks until daybreak, and then he departs (Acts 20:11). Midnight wasn't the end of it. A full night of talking after all that, friends, and I can't even get through a double batch without a nap.

The answer is relieved. The text says the people were greatly relieved to take the boy home alive (Acts 20:12). After what happened, I bet that relief was enormous. Alive is a very good word to hear after a night like that, friends.
